chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad bin Isa, from Hariz bin Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The openhanded and generous one is he who spends his wealth in what is right.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a generous person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this chain to distinguish between mere abundance and true nobility (*karam*), a key virtue in Shia ethics. The hadith clarifies that generosity is validated by its alignment with *haqq* (divine right/justice), implying that spending on frivolous or unjust causes does not constitute true *sakha*. This definition serves as a practical criterion for evaluating charitable acts within the framework of *fiqh* and moral conduct.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad bin Isa, from Huraiz bin Abdullah, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
The openhandedness is the generous who spends his property in rights.
